Description: Creates emergency break-glass accounts excluded from Conditional Access for use when normal admin access is unavailable. Ensures operational continuity during identity infrastructure failures.

Name: Highly privileged role assignments shall be periodically reviewed
Description: Periodically reviews highly privileged role assignments in Entra ID and PIM to verify all privileged access is current and appropriate.

Name: Ensure that between two and four global admins are designated
Description: Ensures between two and four Global Administrators are designated to balance availability with the risk of over-privileged accounts.

Name: Ensure Administrative accounts are cloud-only
Description: Requires administrative accounts to be cloud-only (not synchronized from on-premises AD). Prevents on-premises compromise from directly impacting cloud admin accounts.

Name: Ensure 'Privileged Identity Management' is used to manage roles
Description: Uses Privileged Identity Management (PIM) for all role assignments to provide just-in-time privileged access with approval workflows and time limits.

Name: Ensure approval is required for Global Administrator role activation
Description: Configures PIM to require explicit approval before the Global Administrator role can be activated. Provides an additional control layer for the most powerful role in the tenant.

Name: Ensure external domains are restricted in the Teams admin center
Description: Restricts external domain federation in the Teams admin center to prevent unauthorized external organizations from communicating with internal users.

Name: MFA is enforced on accounts with highly privileged roles
Description: Enforces MFA on all accounts with highly privileged Entra ID roles. Prevents compromised admin credentials from being used without a second factor.

Name: Highly privileged role assignments shall be periodically reviewed Evidence
Description: Provides evidence of periodic review of highly privileged role assignments. Documents that access reviews are being conducted and acted upon.

Name: The number of users with highly privileged roles shall be limited to 4
Description: Limits the number of users with highly privileged roles to a maximum of 4 to minimize the attack surface. Fewer privileged accounts means fewer potential targets for attackers.

Name: Require a temporary access pass to register or join devices
Description: Requires a Temporary Access Pass for users registering authentication methods or joining devices. Provides time-limited, PIN-based access for bootstrapping new users or recovering locked accounts.

Name: Privileged users are assigned a dedicated privileged user account to be used solely for duties requiring privileged access.
Description: Ensures privileged users use dedicated privileged accounts solely for administrative tasks. Prevents administrative work from being performed on accounts used for everyday activities.

Name: Only privileged users responsible for checking that Microsoft Office macros are free of malicious code can write to and modify content within Trusted Locations.
Description: Restricts write access to Microsoft Office Trusted Locations to privileged users responsible for validating macros. Prevents unauthorized addition of trusted locations that bypass macro security.

Name: Privileged users use separate privileged and unprivileged operating environments
Description: Requires privileged users to use separate operating environments for privileged and unprivileged work. Prevents credential exposure from mixing high and low-risk activities.

Name: Unprivileged user accounts cannot logon to privileged operating environments
Description: Prevents unprivileged user accounts from logging into privileged operating environments. Maintains strict separation between administrative and standard user environments.

Name: Privileged access to systems, applications and data repositories is disabled after 12 months unless revalidated
Description: Automatically disables privileged access after 12 months unless explicitly revalidated. Ensures privileged access is periodically reviewed and does not persist indefinitely.

Name: Privileged access to systems and applications is disabled after 45 days of inactivity
Description: Automatically disables privileged access after 45 days of inactivity. Prevents dormant privileged accounts from being compromised and used for attacks.

Name: Privileged operating environments are not virtualized within unprivileged operating environments.
Description: Prevents privileged operating environments from being virtualized within unprivileged environments. Ensures privileged VMs are isolated from potentially compromised unprivileged hosts.

Name: Administrative activities are conducted through jump servers.
Description: Requires administrative activities to be conducted through dedicated jump servers. Provides a controlled, audited path for administrative access to critical systems.

Name: No Admin or Administrator usernames exist
Description: Verifies that no accounts use 'Admin' or 'Administrator' as usernames to prevent easy targeting by attackers using default credential attacks.

Name: Ensure employee accounts do not have administrative privileges
Description: Ensures standard employee accounts do not have administrative privileges in Entra ID or local devices. Enforces least-privilege by separating admin from user accounts.

Name: Ensure administrative accounts use licenses with a reduced application footprint
Description: Ensures administrative accounts use Microsoft 365 licenses with a reduced application footprint (no Exchange, no Teams). Limits the attack surface of admin accounts.

Name: Ensure emergency access account activity is monitored
Description: Configures monitoring and alerting on emergency break-glass account activity to detect unauthorized use. Unusual break-glass activity indicates a potential security incident.

Name: Ensure 'Restrict non-admin users from creating tenants' is set to 'Yes'
Description: Restricts non-admin users from creating new Entra ID tenants to prevent shadow tenant creation that could be used for malicious purposes.

Name: Ensure access to the Entra admin center is restricted
Description: Restricts access to the Entra admin center to privileged administrators only via Conditional Access. Prevents standard users from accessing identity administration features.

Name: Ensure the admin consent workflow is enabled
Description: Enables the admin consent workflow to provide a structured process for users to request consent for applications. Ensures app consent requests are reviewed rather than automatically denied.

Name: Ensure approval is required for Privileged Role Administrator activation
Description: Configures PIM to require explicit approval before the Privileged Role Administrator role can be activated. Provides dual control over the most sensitive role management permissions.

Name: Ensure the GA role is not added as a local administrator during Entra join
Description: Configures Entra ID device join settings to not automatically add the Global Administrator role as a local administrator. Prevents GA role from having unnecessary local admin rights.

Name: Ensure local administrator assignment is limited during Entra join
Description: Limits local administrator assignment during Entra join to specific authorized users. Prevents all users from receiving local admin rights during device enrollment.

Name: Ensure Local Administrator Password Solution is enabled
Description: Enables the Microsoft Entra Local Administrator Password Solution (LAPS) to manage local administrator passwords. Duplicate control reinforcing LAPS enablement.

Name: The vulnerability management dashboard is periodically reviewed
Description: Periodically reviews the Microsoft Defender for Endpoint vulnerability management dashboard to identify and prioritize unpatched vulnerabilities across the device fleet.

Name: A vulnerability management process is defined for Microsoft Defender and Entra ID
Description: Defines a formal vulnerability management process for Microsoft Defender and Entra ID findings. Establishes consistent procedures for vulnerability identification, prioritization, and remediation.

Name: A remediation process is defined for vulnerabilities detected in Microsoft Defender
Description: Defines a remediation process for vulnerabilities detected by Microsoft Defender. Establishes SLAs and workflows for addressing identified vulnerabilities.

Name: Windows Update Rings shall be configured for Windows Devices
Description: Configures Windows Update rings in Microsoft Intune to control the timing and scope of Windows updates across the device fleet. Balances security update speed with operational stability.

Name: Update Policies shall be configured for Apple Devices
Description: Configures update policies for Apple (iOS/macOS) devices via Intune to ensure timely installation of security updates. Maintains Apple device security patch levels.

Name: Authorized Applications should be deployed and updated on managed devices
Description: Deploys and automatically updates authorized applications on managed devices via Intune. Ensures applications are kept current and unauthorized software is prevented.

Name: Secure Score Recommendations shall be monitored and implemented
Description: Monitors Microsoft Secure Score recommendations and implements improvements. Provides a continuous improvement framework for organizational security posture.

Name: Patches, updates or other vendor mitigations for vulnerabilities in office productivity suites, web browsers and their extensions, email clients, PDF software, and security products are applied within 48 hours of release when vulnerabilities are assessed as critical by vendors or when working exploits exist.
Description: Ensures critical patches for office productivity suites, browsers, email clients, PDF software, and security products are applied within 48 hours of release. Aligns with ACSC Essential Eight maturity requirements.

Name: Patches, updates or other vendor mitigations for vulnerabilities in operating systems of workstations, non-internet-facing servers and non-internet-facing network devices are applied within 48 hours of release when vulnerabilities are assessed as critical by vendors or when working exploits exist.
Description: Ensures critical patches for operating systems of workstations and non-internet-facing servers are applied within 48 hours of release. Critical vulnerabilities with working exploits must be remediated urgently.

Name: Patches, updates or other vendor mitigations for vulnerabilities in online services are applied within two weeks of release when vulnerabilities are assessed as non-critical by vendors and no working exploits exist.
Description: Ensures non-critical patches for online services are applied within two weeks of release. Maintains current patch levels for cloud services within an acceptable risk window.

Name: Patches, updates or other vendor mitigations for vulnerabilities in office productivity suites, web browsers and their extensions, email clients, PDF software, and security products are applied within two weeks of release when vulnerabilities are assessed as non-critical by vendors and no working exploits exist.
Description: Ensures non-critical patches for office productivity suites, browsers, and security products are applied within two weeks of release. Maintains endpoint software currency.

Name: Patches, updates or other vendor mitigations for vulnerabilities in operating systems of workstations, non-internet-facing servers and non-internet-facing network devices are applied within two weeks of release when vulnerabilities are assessed as non-critical by vendors and no working exploits exist.
Description: Ensures non-critical patches for operating systems of workstations and non-internet-facing servers are applied within two weeks of release.

Name: Patches, updates or other vendor mitigations for vulnerabilities in operating systems of workstations, non-internet-facing servers and non-internet-facing network devices are applied within one month of release.
Description: Ensures patches for operating systems of workstations and non-internet-facing servers are applied within one month of release at minimum.

Name: Patches, updates or other vendor mitigations for vulnerabilities in applications other than office productivity suites, web browsers and their extensions, email clients, PDF software, and security products are applied within one month of release.
Description: Ensures patches for other applications not in the critical software categories are applied within one month of release.

Name: The latest release, or the previous release, of operating systems are used.
Description: Ensures only the latest or previous release of operating systems are in use across the organization. Running outdated OS versions exposes systems to known vulnerabilities.

Name: Online services that are no longer supported by vendors are removed.
Description: Removes online services no longer supported by vendors to eliminate exposure to unpatched vulnerabilities. Unsupported services will never receive security updates.

Name: Patches, updates or other vendor mitigations for vulnerabilities in online services are applied within 48 hours of release when vulnerabilities are assessed as critical by vendors or when working exploits exist.
Description: Ensures critical patches for online services are applied within 48 hours of release when vulnerabilities are assessed as critical or have working exploits.

Name: Office productivity suites, web browsers and their extensions, email clients, PDF software, Adobe Flash Player, and security products that are no longer supported by vendors are removed
Description: Removes unsupported productivity software, browsers, email clients, PDF software, and security products. Prevents use of applications that no longer receive security updates.

Name: Applications other than office productivity suites, web browsers and their extensions, email clients, PDF software, Adobe Flash Player, and security products that are no longer supported by vendors are removed.
Description: Removes other applications no longer supported by vendors to eliminate exposure to unpatched vulnerabilities across the full application catalog.

Name: Patches, updates or other vendor mitigations for vulnerabilities in operating systems of internet-facing servers and internet-facing network devices are applied within 48 hours of release when vulnerabilities are assessed as critical by vendors or when working exploits exist
Description: Ensures critical patches for internet-facing servers and network devices are applied within 48 hours of release. Internet-facing systems are the highest priority for patching.

Name: Patches, updates or other vendor mitigations for vulnerabilities in operating systems of internet-facing servers and internet-facing network devices are applied within two weeks of release when vulnerabilities are assessed as non-critical by vendors and no working exploits exist
Description: Ensures non-critical patches for internet-facing servers and network devices are applied within two weeks of release. Maintains patching currency for high-exposure systems.

Name: Operating systems that are no longer supported by vendors are replaced
Description: Replaces operating systems no longer supported by vendors to eliminate systemic vulnerability exposure. Unsupported OS versions cannot be secured through patching alone.

Name: A vulnerability scanner is used at least fortnightly to identify missing patches or updates for vulnerabilities in drivers.
Description: Uses a vulnerability scanner at least fortnightly to identify missing driver patches. Driver vulnerabilities can enable privilege escalation and kernel-level attacks.

Name: A vulnerability scanner is used at least fortnightly to identify missing patches or updates for vulnerabilities in firmware
Description: Uses a vulnerability scanner at least fortnightly to identify missing firmware patches. Firmware vulnerabilities can persist through OS reinstallation and enable persistent access.

Name: Patches, updates or other vendor mitigations for vulnerabilities in drivers are applied within 48 hours of release when vulnerabilities are assessed as critical by vendors or when working exploits exist
Description: Ensures critical driver patches are applied within 48 hours of release. Driver vulnerabilities with working exploits must be remediated urgently.

Name: Patches, updates or other vendor mitigations for vulnerabilities in drivers are applied within one month of release when vulnerabilities are assessed as non-critical by vendors and no working exploits exist
Description: Ensures non-critical driver patches are applied within one month of release to maintain driver currency.

Name: Patches, updates or other vendor mitigations for vulnerabilities in firmware are applied within 48 hours of release when vulnerabilities are assessed as critical by vendors or when working exploits exist
Description: Ensures critical firmware patches are applied within 48 hours of release. Firmware vulnerabilities are particularly dangerous due to their persistence and low-level access.

Name: Ensure all servers are updated and patched
Description: Ensures all servers are kept updated and patched with current security updates. Server patching is fundamental to maintaining organizational security posture.

Name: Ensure all public internet facing resources are regularly scanned for vulnerabilities
Description: Regularly scans all public internet-facing resources for vulnerabilities to identify and remediate exposures before attackers can exploit them.

Name: Conduct penetration, vulnerability and social engineering testing
Description: Conducts penetration testing, vulnerability scanning, and social engineering testing to validate security controls. Provides assurance that security controls are effective.

Name: Applications Are Patched Within 14 Days of Critical or High-Risk Updates
Description: Ensures all applications are patched within 14 days of critical or high-risk update releases. Reduces the window of exposure for significant vulnerabilities.

Name: Microsoft 365 Apps are centrally deployed and updated
Description: Deploys and updates Microsoft 365 Apps centrally via Intune or Microsoft 365 Apps admin center. Ensures consistent, timely application of Microsoft 365 application updates.
